mainTopic: The ברכה over fire after שבת and יום הכפורים, and when fire (ours and גיהנם's) was created
overview: This amud opens by finishing a story: עולא silently disagreed with a report of רבי יוחנן's view, and רבה בר בר חנה understood him. Their view is that we bless over fire both after שבת and after יום הכפורים. A ברייתא seems to limit the ברכה to מוצאי שבת, because fire was first created then. The גמרא answers that after יום הכפורים we bless only on fire that 'rested', while brand-new fire from wood or stones is blessed only on מוצאי שבת. The גמרא then asks whether fire was really created on מוצאי שבת, since a ברייתא lists fire among things made on ערב שבת. After several rounds, the conclusion is this: the space of גיהנם came before the world, and its fire came on day two. Our fire was planned on ערב שבת and made on מוצאי שבת, when אדם הראשון rubbed two stones together. A side discussion about the first mule leads to a teaching that ענה was born of a forbidden relationship. The amud ends by quoting in full the ברייתא of ten things created at בין השמשות, whose list of extra opinions continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse describing עולא and רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies משלי 20:5 to עולא, who hinted at his opinion, and to רבה בר בר חנה, who understood the hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But a man of understanding will draw it out.' 'Counsel in a man's heart is deep water' refers to עולא. 'But a man of understanding will draw it out' refers to רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a פסוק and explains who each half of it describes. עולא kept his opinion inside, and רבה בר בר חנה 'drew it out' by understanding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רבי אבא reported a ruling of רבי יוחנן about blessing on fire after יום הכפורים. עולא stood up silently to show he disagreed, and רבה בר בר חנה understood that silent protest. The פסוק praises both people: one held deep thoughts, the other was wise enough to grasp them.

keyTerms.meaning: deep waters (a picture of hidden, deep thoughts)
counsel, an idea or opinion
a man of understanding
will draw it out (like drawing water from a well)

steps.confusionAlert: The first words of this passage are the end of a פסוק that began earlier. The פסוק is then quoted again in two halves so the גמרא can explain each half.

phrases.english: but a man of understanding will draw it out.
phrases.notes: This finishes the פסוק that started a little earlier (משלי כ:ה).

phrases.english: 'Counsel in a man's heart is like deep water'
this is Ulla.
phrases.notes: He had an opinion but did not say it out loud.

phrases.english: 'But a man of understanding will draw it out'
this is Rabba bar bar Ḥana.
phrases.notes: He understood עולא's hint without being told.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַיִם עֲמוּקִּים עֵצָה בְלֶב אִישׁ זֶה עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story earlier about עולא's silent protest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is applied to עולא (the deep thinker) and רבה בר בר חנה (the one who understood him).

steps.title: Whose view did עולא and רבה בר בר חנה hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion led עולא and רבה בר בר חנה to reject רבי אבא's report.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to whom did they hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what opinion עולא and רבה בר בר חנה followed. This question sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know they disagreed with the report of רבי יוחנן's view, but not why. The גמרא wants the source of their own position.

keyTerms.meaning: they (here, עולא and רבה בר בר חנה)
according to whom did they hold it?

phrases.english: And they, in accordance with whom did they hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִינְהוּ כְּמַאן סַבְרוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to the halachic reason behind עולא's reaction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic opinion underlies עולא's and רבה בר בר חנה's rejection of רבי אבא's report?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: bless over fire after שבת and after יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: They hold like רבי בנימין בר יפת's report that רבי יוחנן said we bless over fire both after שבת and after יום הכפורים, and that is the people's practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי יוחנן: We bless over fire both at the end of שבת and at the end of יום הכפורים. And that is how the people act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. עולא and רבה בר בר חנה held a different report of רבי יוחנן: the ברכה on fire is said after both שבת and יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this report, the ברכה after יום הכפורים does not depend on יום הכפורים falling on שבת. It is said every year. The words 'וכן עמא דבר' add that this was the accepted practice.

keyTerms.meaning: we recite a blessing over fire (בורא מאורי האש)
the end of שבת, Saturday night
the end of יום הכפורים
and so the people practice

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for saying בורא מאורי האש in הבדלה after יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת
phrases.english: Like that which Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
One recites a blessing over fire
both at the conclusion of Shabbat
and at the conclusion of Yom Kippur.
And that is how the people act.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They followed רבי יוחנן as reported by רבי בנימין בר יפת: bless over fire after both שבת and יום הכפורים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says fire is blessed only after שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the ברכה on fire is said only after שבת, and רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה in that ברייתא, which seems to contradict his statement in step 3.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: We bless over fire only at the end of שבת, because that is when it was first created. As soon as one sees it, he blesses right away. רבי יהודה says: He arranges the blessings over the cup. And רבי יוחנן said: The halacha follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement from step 3 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא limits the fire ברכה to the end of שבת only, and רבי יוחנן himself ruled like רבי יהודה in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's reason is that fire was first created on מוצאי שבת, when אדם הראשון made fire. That reason does not apply to יום הכפורים. רבי יהודה disagrees only about timing (wait and say it over the הבדלה cup), not about the only-after-שבת rule. So when רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה, he seems to accept 'only after שבת,' which clashes with his own ruling that we also bless after יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: they objected (a challenge from a ברייתא)
the beginning of its creation
he arranges them (the blessings) over the cup of הבדלה
the halacha follows...

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה argues only about WHEN to say the ברכה, not about which nights. So the ruling like רבי יהודה still seems to include 'only after שבת.' That is why it is a problem for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הָאוּר אֶלָּא בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: One recites a blessing over fire only at the conclusion of Shabbat,
since that is the time of its original creation.
And once he sees it, he blesses immediately.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, סוֹדְרָן עַל הַכּוֹס.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He arranges them over the cup.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement of רבי יוחנן brought in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that we bless over fire after יום הכפורים too.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה in a ברייתא that limits the fire ברכה to מוצאי שבת. That makes his two rulings contradict each other.

steps.title: Two kinds of fire: fire that rested and newly made fire
steps.stepSummary: After יום הכפורים we bless over fire that 'rested,' meaning it was lit permissibly. The 'only after שבת' rule is about new fire made from wood or stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means fire that rested; there it means fire produced from wood and from stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that each ruling is about a different kind of fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fire that rested' was not lit in a forbidden way on the holy day, for example it burned from before the day began. Such fire can be blessed after יום הכפורים. Brand-new fire, made by rubbing wood or striking stones, recalls the first creation of fire, so it is blessed only on מוצאי שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult
here... there (each source is about a different case)
fire that 'rested': fire not lit through a forbidden act on the holy day

keyTerms.term: אוּר הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵצִים וּמִן הָאֲבָנִים
keyTerms.meaning: new fire produced from wood or stones

steps.whatToRemember: After יום הכפורים: bless only on אור ששבת. New fire from wood or stones: bless only on מוצאי שבת, because it recalls the creation of fire.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of using a flame that burned throughout יום הכפורים for הבדלה.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
Here, it refers to fire that rested,
phrases.notes: This explains רבי יוחנן's ruling to bless after יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּאוּר הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵצִים וּמִן הָאֲבָנִים.
phrases.english: there, it refers to fire generated from wood and from stones.
phrases.notes: This explains the ברייתא's 'only after שבת.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בְּאוּר שֶׁשָּׁבַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling refers to a different kind of fire.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seemed to be about all fire, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fire that rested is blessed after יום הכפורים. New fire is blessed only after שבת.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about new fire
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says we bless over fire made from wood and stones, and another says we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא taught: Fire produced from wood and stones, we bless over it. Another ברייתא taught: We do not bless over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other about new fire. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the category just defined in step 5. The question is whether new fire from wood or stones gets a ברכה at all, since the sources seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: one ברייתא teaches
and another ברייתא teaches

phrases.english: It was taught in one baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אוּר הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵצִים וּמִן הָאֲבָנִים
phrases.english: fire generated from wood and from stones,
one recites a blessing over it;
and it was taught in another: one does not recite a blessing over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the category of new fire from step 5 and raises a contradiction between ברייתות about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about new fire made from wood and stones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא says to bless over such fire and the other says not to, which is a direct contradiction.

steps.title: New fire: bless after שבת, not after יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says to bless is about מוצאי שבת. The one that says not to bless is about מוצאי יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is at the end of שבת; there it is at the end of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New fire recalls the first creation of fire, which happened on מוצאי שבת, so it is blessed only then. After יום הכפורים there is no such reason, so new fire gets no ברכה. This matches the answer in step 5.
steps.whatToRemember: New fire from wood or stones is blessed on מוצאי שבת but not on מוצאי יום הכפורים. On מוצאי יום הכפורים, only fire that rested is blessed.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
here, it refers to the conclusion of Shabbat,
there, it refers to the conclusion of Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time: each ברייתא refers to a different night.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to argue about new fire in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: New fire is blessed on מוצאי שבת but not on מוצאי יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Two ways of saying the blessings on fire and spices
steps.stepSummary: רבי said the blessings separately when each chance came. רבי חייא gathered them all together into הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי would spread the blessings out. רבי חייא would gather them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports two different practices for the blessings over fire and spices on מוצאי שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said each blessing at its own moment, for example the fire blessing when he first saw a flame. רבי חייא waited and said all of them together over the cup of הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreads them out, saying each blessing separately
Gathers them, saying all the blessings together
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi would distribute them (the blessings).
phrases.notes: He said each blessing when its chance came.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya would collect them.
phrases.notes: He said them all together at הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מְפַזְּרָן רַבִּי חִיָּיא מְכַנְּסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the two sides of the step 4 dispute in practice: רבי blessed right away (like the first opinion), and רבי חייא collected the blessings over the cup (like רבי יהודה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two valid practices: saying each blessing separately (רבי) or saying them all together in הבדלה (רבי חייא).

steps.title: Even רבי repeated the blessings over the cup for his family
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי explains that רבי also said the blessings again over the cup so his household would fulfill their obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: even though רבי spread the blessings out, he would say them again in order over the cup, so that his children and household would fulfill their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a detail that narrows the gap between רבי and רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי had already said the blessings for himself. He repeated them at הבדלה only so that his family could hear and be יוצא. So in the end, the blessings were said over the cup in both homes.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back and arranges them again
The cup of wine used for הבדלה
To help others fulfill their obligation
Members of his household

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
Even though Rabbi distributes them,
he goes back and arranges them over the cup,
in order to fulfill the obligation of his children and household.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבִּי מְפַזְּרָן חוֹזֵר וְסוֹדְרָן עַל הַכּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רבי's practice from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even someone who already said the blessings repeats them over the cup so his household can be יוצא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that saying a blessing again so others can fulfill their obligation is proper, even after you are already יוצא yourself.

steps.title: Challenge: wasn't fire created before שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea that fire was created on מוצאי שבת. It quotes a ברייתא listing ten things created at בין השמשות on the first ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was fire really created on מוצאי שבת? But a ברייתא teaches: ten things were created on ערב שבת at twilight: the well, the מן, the rainbow, writing, the writing tool, the לוחות, משה's grave, the cave where משה and אליהו stood, the opening of the donkey's mouth, and the opening of the earth's mouth to swallow the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that we bless on fire after שבת because fire was first created then. It starts quoting a ברייתא that will show fire was created before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire blessing on מוצאי שבת is tied to the idea that fire was first made then. The ברייתא lists miraculous things made at the very end of the six days of creation. The list here does not mention fire yet. Fire is added in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Was created
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
Twilight, between day and night
The opening of the mouth of בלעם's donkey

phrases.english: And was fire created on Motzaei Shabbat?
But wasn't it taught:
Ten things were created
on Shabbat eve at twilight,
these are: the well, the manna, and the rainbow,
phrases.notes: The well is מרים's well in the desert.

phrases.english: writing, the writing instrument, and the tablets,
and the grave of Moshe,
and the cave in which Moshe and Eliyahu stood,
the opening of the donkey's mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וּפְתִיחַת פִּי הָאָרֶץ לִבְלוֹעַ אֶת הָרְשָׁעִים.
phrases.english: and the opening of the earth's mouth to swallow the wicked.
phrases.notes: קרח and his followers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוּר בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת אִיבְּרִי וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from how the blessing is said to the reason behind it, namely when fire was created.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that fire was first created on מוצאי שבת, which is the basis for blessing on new fire then.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of things created at בין השמשות of ערב שבת will include fire, so fire existed before שבת.

steps.title: The ברייתא adds fire to the list
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי נחמיה adds fire and the mule, and רבי יאשיה adds the ram and the שמיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says in his father's name: also fire and the mule. רבי יאשיה says in his father's name: also the ram and the שמיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted ברייתא continues with more opinions. רבי נחמיה's view, that fire was created on ערב שבת, is the actual source of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the line that clashes with fire being created on מוצאי שבת. The other additions, the mule, the ram of the עקדה, and the שמיר worm, are other special creations from the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his father
Mule, a cross-bred animal
The ram offered by אברהם in place of יצחק
A worm that could cut stone

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says in the name of his father:
Also fire and the mule.
phrases.notes: These are the words the challenge hangs on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya says in the name of his father:
Also the ram and the shamir.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו אַף הָאוּר וְהַפֶּרֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 10 and supplies the clause that mentions fire.
steps.kashyaTarget: Fire being created on מוצאי שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה explicitly lists fire among the things made on ערב שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds tongs and explains why
steps.stepSummary: Within the ברייתא, רבי יהודה adds tongs. He reasons that tongs are made with tongs, so the first pair must have come from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: also the tongs. He used to say: tongs are made using tongs. So who made the first tongs? It must have been made by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יהודה, who adds tongs to the list and gives a logical reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blacksmith needs tongs to hold hot metal while forging new tongs. That leads to the question of where the very first pair came from. רבי יהודה concludes that Heaven must have made it.

keyTerms.meaning: Tongs used by a smith
The first one
Indeed, so it must be
By the hand of Heaven

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Also the tongs.
He used to say:
Tongs are made with tongs,
so who made the first tongs?

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָאיֵ בְּרִיָּה בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם הִיא.
phrases.english: Indeed, it was a creation by the hand of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אַף הַצְּבָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with another addition to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first tongs were made by Heaven at בין השמשות, since tongs require tongs to be made.

steps.title: A challenger: people could make the first tongs
steps.stepSummary: Someone answers רבי יהודה that tongs could be cast in a mold, so the first pair could have been made by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said to him: it is possible to make tongs in a mold and set them straight. So it was a creation by people.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, an unnamed speaker pushes back on רבי יהודה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's argument depends on tongs needing other tongs. The challenger shows another method, pouring metal into a mold, so the first tongs need not be a miracle. This is a side point. The main issue, fire being listed, still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
A mold
By human hands

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is possible to make it in a mold
and align it (set it straight).
phrases.notes: The metal is cast in a mold and then straightened, so no other tongs are needed.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָאיֵ בְּרִיָּה בִּידֵי אָדָם הִיא.
phrases.english: Indeed, it is a creation by human hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֶפְשָׁר יַעֲשֶׂנָּה בִּדְפוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's reasoning in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי יהודה's addition of tongs, not the rest of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that tongs can only be made with tongs is false, since a mold works.
steps.confusionAlert: The tongs debate is a side discussion inside the quoted ברייתא. The גמרא's actual challenge is from fire being on the list (step 11), and it continues in the next step.

steps.title: Two kinds of fire: ours and גיהנם's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our fire was created on מוצאי שבת, while the fire of גיהנם was created on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's not difficult. One source speaks of our fire, and the other speaks of the fire of גיהנם. Our fire was made on מוצאי שבת. The fire of גיהנם was made on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying the two sources are talking about different fires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה's fire on ערב שבת is the fire of גיהנם. Ordinary fire, the one we bless on, was first made on מוצאי שבת. So the reason for the מוצאי שבת blessing still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; introduces an answer
Our fire, ordinary fire
The fire of גיהנם

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about our fire,
that is about the fire of Gehinnom.
Our fire was created on Motzaei Shabbat,
the fire of Gehinnom on Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּאוּר דִּידַן הָא בְּאוּר דְּגֵיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 10–11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the subject: two different kinds of fire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak of the same fire, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ordinary fire came on מוצאי שבת, and the fire of גיהנם on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Challenge: wasn't גיהנם created before the world?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how גיהנם's fire could be from ערב שבת, quoting a ברייתא that גיהנם was among seven things created before the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the fire of גיהנם really made on ערב שבת? But a ברייתא teaches: seven things were created before the world: תורה, תשובה, גן עדן, גיהנם, the כסא הכבוד, the בית המקדש, and the name of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer from step 14 with another ברייתא. The ברייתא's proofs continue in steps 16–17, and step 18 answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If גיהנם existed before creation, its fire seemingly could not first appear on ערב שבת at the end of creation. So the split between the two fires now needs defending.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the world was created
The Throne of Glory
Repentance
The place of punishment for the wicked

phrases.english: And was the fire of Gehinnom created on Shabbat eve?
But wasn't it taught:
Seven things were created
before the world was created,
and these are: Torah, and repentance,
and the Garden of Eden, and Gehinnom,
and the Throne of Glory, and the Temple,
and the name of Mashiach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוּר דְּגֵיהִנָּם בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת אִיבְּרִי וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the fire of גיהנם was created on ערב שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says גיהנם was created before the world, which seems to place its fire long before ערב שבת.

steps.title: Sources for תורה, תשובה, and גן עדן being created before the world
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק for each item on its list. It starts with תורה, תשובה, and גן עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: תורה was created before the world, as it says: 'ה׳ made me the beginning of His way.' תשובה was created before the world, as it says: 'Before the mountains were born,' and right after that it says: 'You bring man down to being crushed, and You say: Return, people.' גן עדן was created before the world, as it says: 'ה׳ planted a garden in Eden, מִקֶּדֶם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from step 15, which lists seven things created before the world. Here it gives a פסוק as proof for each of the first three items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק hints that its item came 'first' or 'before.' For תורה, it is 'the beginning of His way.' For תשובה, it is the פסוק placed right after 'before the mountains were born.' For גן עדן, the word מִקֶּדֶם is read as מִקּוֹדֶם, meaning 'from before.' These proofs build up the list that will soon create the problem with גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'made me' or 'acquired me.' In the פסוק, the תורה is the one speaking.
The beginning of His way, meaning the first thing ה׳ made
Repentance, returning to ה׳
Before
Usually 'in the east,' but here read as 'from before'

steps.confusionAlert: These proofs are not a new topic. They are the second half of the ברייתא that the גמרא started quoting as a challenge in step 15.

phrases.english: Torah, as it is written:
'ה׳ made me as the beginning of His way.'
phrases.notes: משלי ח:כב. The surrounding פסוקים show that the תורה is the one speaking.

phrases.english: Repentance, as it is written:
'Before the mountains were brought forth,'
phrases.notes: תהלים צ:ב

phrases.english: and it is written: 'You return man to contrition,'
'and You say: Repent, children of man.'
phrases.notes: תהלים צ:ג. Because it sits right next to 'before the mountains,' we learn that תשובה existed before the world.

phrases.english: The Garden of Eden, as it is written:
'And ה׳ God planted a garden in Eden, mikedem.'
phrases.notes: בראשית ב:ח. מִקֶּדֶם is read as 'from before' the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 15 by giving the scriptural source for each listed item.
steps.raayaObject: That תורה, תשובה, and גן עדן were created before the world
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי ח:כב; תהלים צ:ב-ג; בראשית ב:ח

steps.title: Sources for גיהנם, the כסא הכבוד, the בית המקדש, and the name of משיח, completing the challenge
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that גיהנם, the כסא הכבוד, the בית המקדש, and the name of משיח were created before the world. This finishes the challenge against the claim that גיהנם's fire was made on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גיהנם was created before the world, as it says: 'For its hearth is set up from yesterday.' The כסא הכבוד and the בית המקדש were created before the world, as it says: 'The Throne of Glory, high from the beginning, is the place of our Sanctuary.' The name of משיח was created before the world, as it says: 'May his name last forever; before the sun, his name existed.' So how can you say גיהנם was made on ערב שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list. The key item is גיהנם, which this ברייתא says existed before the world. That contradicts what the גמרא said in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, the גמרא said גיהנם's fire was created on ערב שבת, at the end of the six days of creation. This ברייתא says גיהנם existed before creation even began. The '!' at the end shows the גמרא is pressing the contradiction: which one is true?

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the wicked are punished, described as a place of fire
Its hearth or fire pit, a name for גיהנם
From yesterday, meaning from long ago, before the world
The Throne of Glory, ה׳'s heavenly throne
A name of משיח. The word suggests 'will endure' or 'will flourish.'

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the answer in the next step. The answer teaches that גיהנם has two parts that were created at two different times.

phrases.english: Gehinnom, as it is written:
'For its hearth is set up from yesterday (of old).'
phrases.notes: ישעיה ל:לג. This is the item that creates the contradiction.

phrases.english: The Throne of Glory and the Temple, as it is written:
'Throne of Glory, on high from the beginning,'
'the place of our Sanctuary.'
phrases.notes: ירמיה יז:יב

phrases.english: The name of Mashiach, as it is written:
'May his name endure forever;'
'before the sun, Yinon is his name!'
phrases.notes: תהלים עב:יז. The '!' marks the end of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּיהִנָּם, דִּכְתִיב: כִּי עָרוּךְ מֵאֶתְמוּל תׇּפְתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's list and brings the challenge from step 15 to its full force.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 14 that the fire of גיהנם was created on ערב שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא proves from a פסוק that גיהנם existed before the world was created, not on ערב שבת at the end of creation.

steps.title: גיהנם's space came before the world, but its fire came on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the empty space (חלל) of גיהנם was created before the world, while its fire was created on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: the empty space of גיהנם is what was created before the world was created. Its fire was created on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. It splits גיהנם into two parts: the empty space and the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was talking about the space or 'pit' of גיהנם, which existed before creation. Step 14 was talking only about the fire inside it, which was made on ערב שבת. Since the two sources describe different parts of גיהנם, they do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They say.' It introduces an answer given by the scholars.
Its empty space, the hollow or pit of גיהנם
Its fire
The eve of the first שבת, at the end of the six days of creation

steps.whatToRemember: גיהנם has two parts. Its space (חלל) existed before the world. Its fire was made on ערב שבת. Our ordinary fire was made on מוצאי שבת.

phrases.english: They say:
it is its empty space that was created
before the world was created,
and its fire was created on Erev Shabbos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי, חֲלָלָהּ הוּא דְּנִבְרָא קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by explaining that the ברייתא and step 14 refer to different parts of גיהנם.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the subject: the ברייתא refers to the space, and the earlier statement refers to the fire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be talking about the same thing, גיהנם as a whole, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The space of גיהנם existed before creation, and its fire was created on ערב שבת, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Was the fire of גיהנם really made on ערב שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that גיהנם's fire was made on ערב שבת. A ברייתא of רבי יוסי says that fire was made on the second day and never goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was its fire really created on ערב שבת? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: the fire that הקדוש ברוך הוא created on the second day of the week will never be put out. As the פסוק says: 'They will go out and see the corpses of the men who rebelled against Me. Their worm will not die and their fire will not be put out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 18, that גיהנם's fire was made on ערב שבת. It quotes רבי יוסי, who says a never-ending fire was made on the second day of creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 put the fire of גיהנם on ערב שבת. רבי יוסי speaks of a fire made on day two that never goes out, and the פסוק he quotes is about the wicked in גיהנם. So day two seems to be the real date, and that contradicts ערב שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fire (the fire of גיהנם)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
On the second day of the week (day two of creation)
Being put out (extinguished)

phrases.english: And was its fire created on Shabbos eve?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אוּר שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּשֵׁנִי בַּשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: The fire that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created on the second day of the week
will never be extinguished,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְיָצְאוּ וְרָאוּ בְּפִגְרֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים הַפּוֹשְׁעִים בִּי
phrases.english: as it says: 'And they shall go out and look upon the corpses of the men who rebelled against Me;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תוֹלַעְתָּם לֹא תָמוּת וְאִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה״,
phrases.english: for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be put out.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 66:24. This is about the punishment of the wicked, which is the fire of גיהנם.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוּר דִּידֵיהּ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת אִיבְּרִי? וְהַתַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 18, which placed גיהנם's fire on ערב שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the fire of גיהנם was created on ערב שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the never-ending fire (גיהנם's fire) was created on the second day, not on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Why day two does not say 'it was good'
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה explains that the תורה leaves out 'כי טוב' on day two because the fire of גיהנם was made that day. This backs up the claim that גיהנם's fire comes from day two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי בנאה, son of רבי עולא, said: Why is 'that it was good' not said about the second day? Because the fire of גיהנם was created on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another source that strengthens the challenge. רבי בנאה clearly says that the fire of גיהנם was created on day two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי did not name גיהנם outright, but רבי בנאה does. He explains the missing 'כי טוב' on day two by saying גיהנם's fire was made then. This makes the contradiction with ערב שבת very sharp.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That it was good' (said about most days of creation)
For what reason? Why?
The fire of גיהנם

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי בְּנָאָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Bena'ah, son of Rabbi Ulla, said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״כִּי טוֹב״ בְּשֵׁנִי בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: Why is 'that it was good' not said on the second day of the week?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּבְרָא בּוֹ אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם.
phrases.english: Because the fire of Gehinnom was created on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי בְּנָאָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 19 with a statement that names גיהנם outright.
steps.raayaObject: That גיהנם's fire was created on the second day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The missing 'כי טוב' on day two in בראשית.

steps.title: Day two is included in 'very good' on day six
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds that day two's creations are still called good. They are included in 'very good' on the sixth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Even though 'that it was good' was not said about it, the תורה went back and included it on the sixth day. As it says: 'And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side comment that came along with רבי בנאה's statement. It explains that day two is not left out of 'good' forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not change the challenge. Day two is still the day of גיהנם's fire. He only adds that the words 'all that He had made... very good' on day six cover day two's creations as well.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and included it
On the sixth day
Very good

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ ״כִּי טוֹב״,
phrases.english: Even though 'that it was good' was not said about it,
He went back and included it on the sixth day,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
phrases.english: as it says: 'And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An add-on to רבי בנאה's statement that came along with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day two's creations are included in the 'very good' of day six.

steps.title: גיהנם's space came first and its fire came on day two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises its answer. The חלל of גיהנם was created before the world, and its fire was created on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: its empty space was made before the world was created, and its fire was made on the second day of the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier claim that גיהנם's fire was made on ערב שבת. It now puts that fire on day two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split from step 18 between the space and the fire stays. The space came before the world, which fits the list of seven things. Only the date of the fire moves, from ערב שבת to day two, which fits רבי יוסי and רבי בנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we must change our earlier answer)
Its empty space (the space of גיהנם)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. Step 18 said the fire came on ערב שבת. That is now replaced: the fire came on day two. Only the space came before the world.

phrases.english: Rather: its void was before the world was created,
and its fire was on the second day of the week.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: חֲלָלָהּ — קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 19 and 20 by changing the date of the fire.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Revised answer (אלא): it keeps the split between space and fire but changes the date of the fire.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought גיהנם's fire was created on ערב שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The space of גיהנם came before the world, and its fire came on day two.

steps.title: Our fire was planned on ערב שבת but made on מוצאי שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how ערב שבת still connects to fire. Our fire was planned in God's thought on ערב שבת, but it was only actually created on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our fire came up in God's thought to be created on ערב שבת, but it was not created until מוצאי שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that גיהנם's fire has moved to day two, the גמרא explains where ערב שבת fits. It belongs to our fire, which was only planned then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the idea from step 14 that our fire was created on מוצאי שבת. It also answers the original challenge from רבי נחמיה in step 11, who listed fire among the things of ערב שבת. His list refers to the planning of our fire on ערב שבת, while its actual creation was on מוצאי שבת, so the reason for blessing on new fire on מוצאי שבת (step 4) still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Our fire (ordinary fire)
It came up in God's thought (it was planned)
The night after שבת ends

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the space of גיהנם came before the world. גיהנם's fire came on day two. Our fire was planned on ערב שבת and made on מוצאי שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for saying a ברכה on fire (בורא מאורי האש) at הבדלה on מוצאי שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וְאוּר דִּידַן — בְּמַחְשָׁבָה עָלָה לִיבָּרְאוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: And our fire arose in thought to be created on Shabbos eve,
but it was not created until the conclusion of Shabbos.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוּר דִּידַן — בְּמַחְשָׁבָה עָלָה לִיבָּרְאוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the revised answer by explaining where ערב שבת fits in. This reinterprets רבי נחמיה's 'אף האור' (step 11) as referring to the planning of our fire.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns ערב שבת: it belongs to the planning of our fire.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ערב שבת was the date גיהנם's fire was made.
steps.terutzMaskana: ערב שבת was when our fire was planned. It was made on מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: אדם הראשון makes fire and the first mule on מוצאי שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי supports this. Two things were planned on ערב שבת and made on מוצאי שבת: fire, which אדם הראשון made from two stones, and the mule.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches, רבי יוסי says: Two things came up in God's thought to be created on ערב שבת, but they were not created until מוצאי שבת. On מוצאי שבת, הקדוש ברוך הוא gave אדם הראשון wisdom similar to the wisdom above. He took two stones and rubbed them against each other, and fire came out of them. He took two animals and crossbred them, and a mule came out of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for what it just said about our fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same words: 'planned on ערב שבת, not created until מוצאי שבת'. Fire is one of the two things, which proves step 23. The second thing is the mule, which leads to the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Adam, the first man
Knowledge, understanding
Like the model above (similar to divine wisdom)
Crossbred
Mule

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים עָלוּ בְּמַחְשָׁבָה לִיבָּרְאוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Two things arose in thought to be created on Shabbos eve,
but were not created until the conclusion of Shabbos,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת נָתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא דֵּיעָה בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: and at the conclusion of Shabbos the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave knowledge to Adam, the first man,
similar to the model above,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵבִיא שְׁנֵי אֲבָנִים וּטְחָנָן זוֹ בָּזוֹ,
phrases.english: and he brought two stones and ground them against each other,
and fire came out of them,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת וְהִרְכִּיב זוֹ בָּזוֹ
phrases.english: and he brought two animals and crossbred them with each other,
phrases.notes: A female horse and a male donkey.

phrases.english: and a mule came out of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים עָלוּ בְּמַחְשָׁבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source for step 23.
steps.raayaObject: Our fire was planned on ערב שבת and made on מוצאי שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי about אדם הראשון.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the mule came in ענה's time
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees about the mule. He says the first mule came in the days of ענה, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: The mule came about in the days of ענה. As it says: 'This is ענה, who found the mules in the wilderness.'
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues with רבי יוסי about the mule only. He says ענה, not אדם, brought the first mule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'הימם' as mules. 'Found' is understood to mean that ענה produced them by crossbreeding. The argument here is only about the mule, not about fire.

keyTerms.meaning: ענה, a descendant of שעיר (בראשית 36)
Understood here as 'the mules'

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
The mule came in the days of Anah,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוּא עֲנָה אֲשֶׁר מָצָא אֶת הַיֵּמִם בַּמִּדְבָּר״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'This is Anah who found the mules in the wilderness.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:24.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: פֶּרֶד בִּימֵי עֲנָה הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוסי about when the mule first came about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first mule came in ענה's time, not in אדם's time.

steps.title: ענה was unfit, so he brought an unfit creature
steps.stepSummary: The דורשי חמורות taught that ענה came from a forbidden relationship. So he brought into the world an 'unfit' creature, the mule, which cannot have offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who explained the hidden meanings of the תורה used to say: ענה was unfit, so he brought an unfit creature into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a related teaching about ענה. It makes a claim, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a 'measure for measure' idea here. ענה was born from an forbidden relationship. The creature he produced, the mule, cannot reproduce.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who explain the deep or hidden meanings of the תורה
Unfit or flawed (here: born of a forbidden relationship)
Therefore

phrases.english: The interpreters of hidden meanings used to say:
Anah was unfit,
therefore he brought unfitness into the world,

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוֹרְשֵׁי חֲמוּרוֹת, הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that ענה brought the first mule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ענה was born of a forbidden relationship, so he produced the sterile mule.

steps.title: Two פסוקים show צבעון fathered ענה with his own mother
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק counts ענה as a son of שעיר, and another counts him as a son of צבעון. This shows that צבעון fathered ענה with his own mother, the wife of שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'These are the sons of שעיר the Horite' (and ענה is listed there). And it is written: 'These are the sons of צבעון: איה and ענה.' Rather, this teaches that צבעון came upon his mother and fathered ענה from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim of step 26 by putting two פסוקים side by side that seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ענה is the son of שעיר, he is צבעון's brother. If he is the son of צבעון, he is צבעון's son. Both can be true if צבעון had a child with שעיר's wife, his own mother. That would make ענה both 'from שעיר's house' and צבעון's son.

keyTerms.meaning: שעיר the Horite, father of the clan
צבעון, a son of שעיר
This teaches

phrases.english: as it says: 'These are the sons of Seir the Horite,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:20. Both צבעון and ענה are listed as sons of שעיר.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah'!
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:24. Here ענה is called צבעון's son.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבָּא צִבְעוֹן עַל אִמּוֹ
phrases.english: Rather, this teaches that Zibeon cohabited with his mother
and fathered Anah from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֵלֶּה בְנֵי שֵׂעִיר הַחֹרִי״, וּכְתִיב: ״אֵלֶּה בְנֵי צִבְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim that ענה was unfit.
steps.raayaObject: ענה was born of a forbidden relationship.

steps.title: Maybe there were two people named ענה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. Maybe there were two different people named ענה, one a son of שעיר and one a son of צבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe there were two people named ענה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the proof from step 27. It suggests the פסוקים may be talking about two different men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if both פסוקים mean the same ענה. If there were two men named ענה, there is no contradiction, and so no proof of a forbidden relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Two

phrases.english: But perhaps there were two named Anah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא תְּרֵי עֲנָה הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that both פסוקים refer to the same ענה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there were two people named ענה, the פסוקים do not contradict, so nothing is proven.

steps.title: 'הוא ענה' means the same ענה as before
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or, in another version, רב פפא) answers from the פסוק itself. 'הוא ענה' means it is the same ענה mentioned earlier, so there was only one ענה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I will say something that שבור מלכא did not say. Who is that? שמואל. Some say רב פפא said: I will say something that שבור מלכא did not say. Who is that? רבא. The פסוק says 'הוא ענה', meaning he is the same ענה from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 28. The extra word 'הוא' in the פסוק shows that it is the same ענה, so the proof stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who said the answer. In each one, the speaker says he is offering something that a great sage, nicknamed 'שבור מלכא' (King Shapur), did not say. The answer itself is the same in both: 'הוא' ('he is') points back to the ענה already mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: King Shapur, used as a nickname for a great sage
Some say (a different version)
The פסוק says
From the beginning (the one mentioned earlier)

steps.confusionAlert: שבור מלכא here is not the Persian king. It is an honorary nickname for שמואל (in the first version) or רבא (in the second).
steps.whatToRemember: There was only one ענה. 'הוא ענה' ties the פסוקים together, so the teaching that ענה came from a forbidden relationship stands.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמֵינָא מִילְּתָא דְּשַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא לָא אַמְרַהּ,
phrases.english: Rava said: I will say a matter that King Shapur did not say,
And who is he? Shmuel.
Some say: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמֵינָא מִילְּתָא דְּשַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא לָא אַמְרַהּ,
phrases.english: I will say a matter that King Shapur did not say,
And who is he? Rava.
The verse says: 'This is Anah' —
he is the same Anah from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמֵינָא מִילְּתָא דְּשַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא לָא אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A close reading of the פסוק: the word 'הוא' shows it is the same person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There may have been two men named ענה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הוא ענה' points to the earlier ענה, so there was only one.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists ten things created at בין השמשות before the first שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ten special things were created on the first ערב שבת at בין השמשות, and lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught: Ten things were created on ערב שבת at בין השמשות. These are they: the well, the מן, the rainbow, the writing, the writing tool, the לוחות, משה's grave, the cave where משה and אליהו stood, the opening of the donkey's mouth, and the opening of the earth's mouth to swallow the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists ten miraculous things that were created at the very end of the six days of Creation, right as the first שבת began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is something that showed up later in history as a miracle, like the well in the desert, the מן, or בלעם's talking donkey. The ברייתא teaches that these miracles were not added later. They were built into Creation from the start, in its last moment at בין השמשות. This connects to the earlier steps, which asked when the mule and fire first came into the world.

keyTerms.meaning: The eve of Shabbos, here the sixth day of Creation
Twilight, the in-between moment as day turns into night
The well that traveled with the Jews in the desert (בארה של מרים)
The writing (the shape of the letters on the לוחות) and the tool used to engrave them
The opening of the mouth of בלעם's donkey so it could speak
The earth opening up to swallow קרח and his group

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these things were created by accident or as an afterthought. The point is the opposite. These later miracles were planned and set up at the end of Creation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא teaches a basic idea about miracles. Things that seem to break nature later in history were already prepared inside Creation.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: Ten things were created
on Shabbos eve, at twilight,
phrases.notes: The last moment of the six days of Creation

phrases.english: and these are they: the well, the manna, and the rainbow,
phrases.notes: The well is מרים's well; the rainbow is the sign shown after the מבול

phrases.english: the writing, the writing instrument, and the tablets,
phrases.notes: All connected to the לוחות given at סיני

phrases.english: the grave of Moshe,
and the cave in which Moshe and Eliyahu stood,
phrases.notes: The cleft of the rock at סיני/חורב

phrases.english: the opening of the donkey's mouth,
phrases.notes: בלעם's donkey

phrases.aramaic: וּפְתִיחַת פִּי הָאָרֶץ לִבְלוֹעַ אֶת הָרְשָׁעִים.
phrases.english: and the opening of the earth's mouth to swallow the wicked.
phrases.notes: קרח and his followers

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נִבְרְאוּ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of ענה and the mule, the גמרא now quotes in full the ברייתא of ten things created at בין השמשות. The same list of ten was already quoted as part of the challenge in step 10, and here it continues with further יש אומרים additions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten miraculous things were created at בין השמשות of the first ערב שבת: באר, מן, קשת, כתב, מכתב, לוחות, קברו של משה, the cave of משה and אליהו, the mouth of the donkey, and the mouth of the earth.

steps.title: Other opinions add more items to the list
steps.stepSummary: Several יש אומרים opinions add more items to the twilight list: אהרן's staff with its almonds and blossoms, the מזיקין, and one more item that continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: also אהרן's staff, with its almonds and blossoms. Some say: also the demons. And some say: also... (continued on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings other opinions that add more things to the list of what was created at twilight. The last יש אומרים is cut off, and it continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ten items were the basic list. Now different voices suggest more items. One is אהרן's staff, which blossomed and grew almonds to prove his כהונה. Another is the מזיקין, the harmful spirits. Each יש אומרים adds to the list and does not argue against the earlier items.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, introducing another opinion
Also / even, adding to what was already said
אהרן's staff, which miraculously blossomed
Its almonds and its blossoms
Harmful spirits / demons

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא said 'ten things,' but these opinions add more. That is fine. These are additional views about the list, not a mistake in the count of the main opinion.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מַקְלוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: And some say: also Aharon's staff,
with its almonds and its blossoms,
phrases.notes: The staff blossomed after קרח's rebellion to prove אהרן was chosen

phrases.english: and some say: also the demons,
and some say: also...
phrases.notes: This addition is cut off here and continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מַקְלוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further opinions that expand the ten-item list from step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Additional opinions include אהרן's blossoming staff and the מזיקין among the things created at twilight. Another addition is introduced here and continues on the next amud.
